title: Re-cut Newsreader without the pin that flattened it
summary:
Newsreader was vendored through fontTools.varLib.instancer with opsz pinned at 18, which flattened the axis the design asks for. This binder re-cuts it from the same pinned upstream without that pin, ships one file in place of two, and teaches the readers that treat a face's weight as a single integer to handle a range.

Be precise about what is then verified, because the two are not the same size. The CHANGE is visible in the diff: the recipe loses a pin and the manifest records what it now carries. The CHECK is narrower: the shipped file's table directory reports an fvar entry of the recorded length, and the manifest, the files on disk and the stylesheet agree with each other. Which axes the file carries, what ranges they span, and whether the bytes decode at all are none of them reachable without a font library or a browser, and the floor has neither. Nothing here measures what the page renders; that is briefed in docs/backlog/watch-optical-harness/FINDINGS.md.
motivation:
The gap survived a design comparison, and the reason it survived is worth saying first.

The design (design/Karta Status Design Redesign/Karta Watch.dc.html:13) asks Google Fonts for Newsreader:opsz,wght@6..72,400;6..72,500 — a live optical-size axis from 6 to 72. karta forbids a font CDN, so the faces were vendored same-origin, and each was pinned with fontTools.varLib.instancer before subsetting. Newsreader was pinned at opsz 18, which is the axis default, so the page looks unremarkable and is wrong at five of the six sizes it uses. Verified by parsing the shipped files: no face carries an fvar table.

The comparison could not have caught it. The frozen design reference at docs/designs/karta-watch-1440x900-light.html says so in its own header: it points the mascot and the eight faces at the copies this repo already vendors, and its @font-face block at :35-40 names newsreader-400.woff2 and newsreader-500.woff2. So the design side of every fidelity run has been rendering with the page's own flattened faces. Both sides agreed because both sides were the same font. That is a property of the reference, not a bug this binder can close — see reference-is-not-a-font-instrument below.

How much this shows: the advance width of an 18-character string at 40px moves 13.172 px, measured in Chromium against the real variable subset. That is 4 percent of the line, on the largest headline on the page.

The proof is the hard half, and two rounds of review went into narrowing what each check can honestly claim. A shipped file's fvar table says the face is variable; it does NOT say which axes it carries, because WOFF2 table data is Brotli-compressed and this script is stdlib-only. A face with wght still variable and opsz pinned at 18 — the exact regression — would carry fvar and satisfy any presence check. So the file-level gate is named for what it proves, and the optical-size claim rests entirely on a rendered measurement. Load state is not adherence either: a previous fidelity run recorded document.fonts.status reading 'loaded' while all eight faces returned 404, and document.fonts.check('40px Newsreader') returns true for the wrong face.

One more thing belongs in the record, because it shaped what this binder contains. An earlier draft carried the rendered check as two further items, and thirteen review rounds could not make them safe. The findings stopped being about claims that overreach and became implementation decisions in a measurement system — which API measures a text advance, how many samples make a spread, what turns a separation into a margin, whether a fifty-two character heading at 40px can be measured by a bounding box when it wraps at 1440, whether a synthetic probe can see font-optical-sizing:none set on the real element. Each round pinned some and surfaced more, because a prose specification of a measurement harness has no natural end. The two items here are the part that can be settled before anything is built. The rest is written as work, against the real page, briefed by docs/backlog/watch-optical-harness/FINDINGS.md.

included: skills/karta-status/scripts/serve_status.py and its two mirrors — a stdlib WOFF2 table-directory reader, two new anchored behaviours, the @font-face block, the VENDORED_FACES enumeration and its readers.

skills/karta-status/assets/fonts/ and its two mirrors — the two static Newsreader files are replaced by one unpinned cut; the manifest gains a per-face variation record, the axis record, the fvar table length and the fontTools version.
skills/karta-status/scripts/selftest_behaviours.txt and its two mirrors — two names added, none retired.
docs/designs/karta-watch-1440x900-light.html — the frozen reference's Newsreader @font-face rules, which name files this binder deletes, and a header line recording what the reference cannot prove.

A precondition rather than a change, stated because a reviewer who checks the wrong branch will conclude the binder is broken. Every file:line reference here is against the tree this binder is DELIVERED onto, which is the default branch with watch-drill-in already landed — the dependency the top-level `after` field declares. The two candidate trees genuinely differ and neither one alone satisfies the references: measured, _vendored_weights is at serve_status.py:8258 on the default branch today and :8557 after the merge, _c_vendored_font_faces at :13096 and :14665, the first tabular-nums rule at :1495 and :1531. Meanwhile the design export this binder reads the axis request from lives on the default branch and is NOT on karta/watch-drill-in/integration, and docs/backlog/watch-optical-harness/FINDINGS.md, which assertion 8's caveat points at, is committed alongside this binder. So checking these references against the integration branch in isolation reports missing files, and checking them against the default branch before the merge reports wrong line numbers. Both are artifacts of looking at half the base.
excluded: IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono. Their weights already match the design exactly (400, 500, 600 each) and the wdth:100 pin on Plex Sans was checked rather than assumed: the upstream axis is 75..100 with default 100, and the design requests no wdth at all, so the pin removes nothing the design asks for.

Loading Newsreader from fonts.googleapis.com the way the design does. The page stays same-origin, _c_no_remote_fetch (serve_status.py:14747) keeps holding it there, and the difference in loading mechanism is booked as intended rather than treated as a defect.

THE RENDERED ADHERENCE CHECK, and this is the largest thing left out. Nothing here measures what the browser drew, so nothing here proves the axis being shipped is the OPTICAL-SIZE axis rather than some other variation axis, and nothing proves the page renders at the right optical size. Say the consequence plainly: after this binder the floor knows the shipped file's directory reports a variation-table entry of a recorded size — not that the file is a usable variable font, not which axes it carries, not that it decodes — and a human knows the rest only by looking. That is a real gap and it is deliberate. An earlier draft planned the check as two further items and thirteen review rounds could not make them safe — the open questions were implementation decisions in a measurement harness, and a harness cannot be specified in prose before it exists. The measurements taken while trying are recorded in docs/backlog/watch-optical-harness/FINDINGS.md together with the brief; the work is written against the real page, and the harness it produces defines its own gate.

Reading the axis NAMES or RANGES out of a shipped woff2. WOFF2 table data is Brotli-compressed and the stdlib has no Brotli, so a directory read reaches the presence and recorded size of the fvar table and no further. Adding a font library to the floor would trade a stated dependency rule for a convenience.
Giving the frozen design reference its own pinned copy of the design's fonts. It keeps pointing at the page's faces and now says in its header that it therefore cannot witness a font difference.
Re-capturing the frozen design reference from the live design.

design_facts.stack: Python stdlib http.server + vendored Vue 3 SPA, shipped as a Claude Code / Codex plugin skill

isolation_params: no parameter to inject, but NOT no environment, and the difference is worth stating because an earlier draft of this binder claimed the floor needs nothing. It does. validate_plugin.py's design-serving rig (:569) binds an ephemeral loopback port at :586, spawns the committed page as a subprocess at :588, and requests it over HTTP at :602. So the oracle needs loopback sockets and the ability to spawn a subprocess, and it fails outright where socket creation is prohibited. It picks its own port, so concurrent items do not collide and nothing has to be injected.
what it does NOT need: a browser, a network route off loopback, or a server this binder starts. The rendered check that needed those is not in this binder.

token_manifest.mechanism: Newsreader is one role token, --serif (serve_status.py:1447). What varies across the rows below is the size the role is set at, and the design makes the optical size follow it.
token_manifest.source_of_truth: Sizes are read from the committed design reference docs/designs/karta-watch-1440x900-light.html, the file validate_plugin.py resolves as DESIGN_REFERENCE_REL (:469). The axis request is read from the live export design/Karta Status Design Redesign/Karta Watch.dc.html, because the reference's capture dropped the Google Fonts link. Each row's traced_by names '<item-id>:<0-based assertion index>'. Facts about the RENDERED page — the six serif sizes, the state each needs, the per-element text and the advance measurements — are not in this table because no item here measures them; they live in docs/backlog/watch-optical-harness/FINDINGS.md.
token_manifest.no_new_tokens: no token is added, changed or removed. --serif keeps its name, its family list and its system fallback.

design_fact_table.fact: The design asks for Newsreader:opsz,wght@6..72,400;6..72,500 — a live optical-size axis, 6 to 72, at weights 400 and 500 (design/Karta Status Design Redesign/Karta Watch.dc.html:13). The committed reference capture dropped this link, which is why the axis was invisible to every comparison run against it.

The upstream Newsreader[opsz,wght].ttf the manifest pins carries opsz 6..72 with default 18 and wght 200..800 with default 400 — read during planning from the file at the pinned commit, whose sha256 matches the manifest's recorded source_sha256. Pinning opsz at 18 was pinning it to the axis default, which is why nothing looked obviously broken.

An fvar table means the face carries some variation axis. It does not name the axis, and WOFF2 table data is Brotli-compressed with no stdlib Brotli, so a directory read cannot reach the axis tags. A face with wght variable and opsz pinned at 18 — the exact regression — carries fvar. The file-level gate is therefore named for a variation-axis table, and the optical-size claim is made only by the rendered check.

The frozen design reference declares the page's own vendored faces at docs/designs/karta-watch-1440x900-light.html:35-40 and says so in its header. Both sides of every fidelity run have therefore used the same Newsreader, and repointing the reference at the new single cut preserves that. The reference is not made an independent font witness here; its header is made to say it is not one.
IBM Plex Sans was instanced at wdth 100. The upstream axis is 75..100 with default 100, and the design requests no wdth, so the pin removes nothing the design asks for. Checked rather than assumed.
design_fact_table.untraced_reason: no assertion depends on it — it is the recorded reason IBM Plex Sans and Mono are out of scope, and an assertion about a font this binder does not change would be a claim with no work behind it.

design_fact_table.fact: Built from the pinned upstream during planning: the two-axis cut this binder ships carries an fvar of 84 bytes, the same cut with opsz pinned and wght left variable carries 56, and the cut with both pinned carries no fvar at all. One axis record apart, so a silent opsz flattening changes the recorded length. Read that as a fact about THESE cuts and not about fvar in general: the length pins neither which axes a face carries nor how many, because instance count and the optional postScriptNameID field trade against axis count in the same total. What it catches is this specific flattening, of this upstream, whose instance layout is otherwise unchanged.

The documented flag set produced 79,784 bytes on fontTools 4.60.1 and then 79,948 and 79,648 on two runs of 4.63.0 from the same input. The payload assertion therefore pins the budget bound and records the count, rather than gating a number that moves.

Reproduced during planning: the manifest's existing flags — --unicodes=U+0000-00FF,U+2000-206F --layout-features+=tnum --no-hinting --desubroutinize --flavor=woff2 --name-IDs=1,2,3,4,5,6,16,17 — preserve fvar, gvar, avar, HVAR and STAT with no new flag. The variations were lost to the fontTools.varLib.instancer step, not to the subsetter. Upstream axes read from the pinned file: wght 200..800 default 400, opsz 6..72 default 18.

Read off the integration tree: _vendored_weights has six consumers. Two read the weight set — _c_type_roles_bound at :9657, the faux-bold guard that sweeps every CSS rule, and _c_card_title_serif_step at :14167. Four test only family-key membership — :9028, :9878, :9983, :14128. A range object left unexpanded fails the first two and leaves the other four green, so the headline step is not the check that proves the change landed. The function at :9862 is _c_binder_headline_type_step; there is no _c_binder_headline_serif_step.

An fvar table is 16 bytes plus 20 per axis plus one record per named instance, so axis count trades against instance count. The cut this binder ships is 84 bytes as two axes with two instances; a one-axis face with six instances is 84 as well. The length reliably catches the narrow regression it was chosen for — the same cut with an axis dropped, 84 to 56 — and does not pin the axis count in general.

Probed on all eight shipped faces: STAT appears as literal bytes, and fvar, avar, gvar, cmap and head do not. A WOFF2 known-tag directory entry is a flags byte with a 6-bit index and no tag; only index 63 carries a literal four-byte tag. Recorded because a reviewer proposed the opposite — that the known-tag list carries each tag as a UInt32 — which the probe refutes: cmap and head would then be present.

An fvar table of a recorded length pins none of: which axis tags are present, the ranges on them, the named instances' coordinates, or whether the optional postScriptNameID is present. A narrowed opsz is the nearest example of what slips through, not the shape of the gap. The one thing the length does catch is the same cut of the same upstream with an axis dropped, 84 to 56.

Every check in this binder reads filenames, manifest hashes, table-directory metadata, CSS URLs and byte counts. None decompresses the face or loads it, so bytes with a plausible WOFF2 header and an fvar entry of the recorded length pass while being an unusable font. A decoder needs Brotli or a browser, both outside the floor's dependency rule.

work_items.title: A stdlib reader for the WOFF2 table directory
work_items.summary: Parses a WOFF2 table directory without decompressing anything, returning each table's tag and recorded length, and anchors one behaviour that holds the manifest to what the files say: a face the manifest marks variable has an fvar entry of the recorded length, one it marks static has none. All eight faces are marked static here, which is what they are. The instrument lands before the font so the item that ships the font has something to be judged by. The behaviour is named for a variation-table entry and never for an optical size, because a directory read cannot reach an axis tag.
shared_resources: skills/karta-status/scripts/serve_status.py — every item in this binder edits it; the orchestrator serializes them
skills/karta-status/assets/fonts/manifest.json — this item adds the per-face variation field to all eight entries; the next item changes one of them

contract.exposes: a stdlib WOFF2 table-directory reader inside serve_status.py, returning each table's tag and recorded length without decompressing anything, plus two anchored behaviours. The first is the instrument's own: the reader round-trips a directory that uses a known-tag index and one that uses a literal tag, and raises on a truncated one. The second is the one that holds the line for the rest of the binder: the manifest's per-face variation claim agrees with what that face's directory reports — a face the manifest calls variable lists fvar and records its table length; a face it calls static does not. This item also adds that per-face field to all eight manifest entries, every one of them static, which is what the files say today.
contract.preserves: the stdlib-only, zero-dependency rule the font section is built on (serve_status.py:110-124). No font library is added, nothing is decompressed, and the note at VENDORED_FACES stays true: glyph coverage is still a guarantee of the build step and not something read back out of a woff2. The eight shipped faces are unchanged by this item — it ships an instrument and a record of the current state, not a font.
contract.regression_risk:
two ways to get this wrong, and the item exists partly to write both down.

First, the obvious shortcut is wrong. fvar is a KNOWN WOFF2 table tag — index 47 of the 63-entry list — so it is encoded as a 6-bit index in a flag byte and the four bytes 'fvar' never appear in the file. Measured on the faces shipped today: STAT appears as literal bytes because it is NOT in the known list, while fvar, avar, gvar, cmap and head do not. A known-tag entry is a flags byte carrying a 6-bit index and NO tag; only index 63 is followed by a literal four-byte tag. That is worth stating because the opposite is a natural assumption and a reviewer raised it: were the known-tag entries to carry their tags as well, cmap and head would appear as bytes in every shipped face, and the probe says they do not. A substring scan for 'fvar' therefore reports every variable font as static and would pass silently. The reader has to parse the 48-byte header, then one entry per table with its UIntBase128 lengths.

Second, and this is the finding two independent reviewers raised: fvar means the face carries SOME variation axis. It does not mean opsz. A re-vendor that pins opsz at 18 and leaves wght 400..500 variable writes an fvar table and would satisfy a presence check — and that is the exact regression this binder is guarding. So the behaviour is named for a variation-axis table, never for optical size, and the recorded fvar LENGTH is part of the agreement: an axis added or removed changes the table's size, so a silent flattening fails here and a declared one becomes a visible manifest edit that says which axis went away. The optical-size claim itself is made NOWHERE IN THIS BINDER. Proving the axis is opsz needs a rendered measurement, which is the work briefed in docs/backlog/watch-optical-harness/FINDINGS.md. Until that exists, the honest statement is that the floor knows a variation table is present and its size, and nothing more.
contract.verification_honesty: this item's oracle is the repo floor, which needs no browser and no network OFF LOOPBACK. The qualifier is not pedantry and an earlier draft got it wrong in the other direction: the floor's design-serving rig binds an ephemeral loopback port, spawns the committed page as a subprocess and requests it over HTTP, all recorded in this binder's env_contract. So a bare 'no network' here would contradict that field. What is true is that nothing leaves the machine and no font host is reached. Everything it asserts is read from bytes already in the tree.

assertions: The reader parses a WOFF2 table directory from the 48-byte header onward and returns every table's tag with its recorded length, reading no compressed byte. It gets the transform rule right, which is tag-specific and is the one place a plausible parser silently desynchronises: the flag byte's low six bits are a known-tag index with 63 meaning a literal four-byte tag follows, and its top two bits are the transform version. For glyf and loca, version 0 means TRANSFORMED and a second UIntBase128 length follows, while version 3 is the null transform and none does. For every other table the sense is reversed: 0 is the null transform. Non-zero is not a blanket 'transformed' either — the spec defines version 1 for hmtx and leaves the rest undefined, and an undefined version means the font is invalid and must be REJECTED rather than parsed generically. A reader that treats any non-zero version as a transform will happily read a malformed font and report a table list for it. A reader that tests 'version is non-zero' MISSES a length that is there on a version-0 glyf, and CONSUMES one that is not there on a version-3 table, and from that point every later tag it reports is garbage — while still answering 'no fvar' for all eight faces shipped today, which is the correct answer for the wrong reason. Negative control: fixtures for a known-tag index, a literal tag, a transformed glyf/loca pair placed BEFORE fvar in the directory, a version-3 glyf, and an hmtx at version 1 must each round-trip to the complete ordered tag list with correct lengths; every version the spec does not define must raise rather than round-trip, enumerated rather than sampled — glyf and loca at versions 1 and 2, hmtx at 2 and 3, and any ordinary table at 1, 2 or 3 — because a reader that rejects one reserved value and waves through another passes a single-fixture test while still parsing an invalid font; a directory truncated mid-entry must raise rather than return a short list that reads as a valid answer; a file whose first four bytes are not wOF2 must raise rather than be parsed as one, since every guarantee here starts from that signature and the contract's --flavor=woff2 claim rests on it; and a UIntBase128 in one of the forms the spec declares invalid — a leading 0x80, or a value overflowing 32 bits — must raise rather than decode to something plausible, because a length silently mis-decoded is how a reader reports a confident and wrong tag list.

The check reads the directory and never scans for the bytes 'fvar'. Both halves of that are proven against SYNTHETIC fixtures committed with the test, because the repository's own fonts cannot demonstrate either half — measured on all eight, STAT appears as literal bytes because it is not in the known-tag list, while fvar, avar, gvar, cmap and head never do, and at this point in the binder no shipped face is variable at all. Negative control: a fixture whose compressed data block contains the bytes 'fvar' is reported as carrying no fvar table, and a synthetic variable face that contains those bytes nowhere is reported as carrying one.

An anchored behaviour holds the manifest to what the files say. For every face the manifest marks variable: fvar appears in the directory with a recorded length that both matches the manifest and is non-zero, and every variation table the manifest RECORDS for that face appears with a non-zero recorded origLength. For every face the manifest marks static: no fvar. All eight entries are marked static in this item, so the variable branch is exercised by synthetic fixtures here and by the shipped cut once the next item lands.

The rule reads the manifest rather than naming tags, and that is deliberate. OpenType requires no particular delta table in a variable font — a CFF2 face carries no gvar at all, and a face that varies only its metrics can pair HVAR with fixed outlines — so a behaviour that hardcoded gvar would be wrong in general while happening to be right here. Making the manifest name the tables holds the file to what the recipe claims to have preserved, and leaves the question of which tags THIS cut must carry to the item that ships it.

Why the delta tables are in the rule at all, since fvar presence is the obvious check and is not enough: fvar DECLARES the axes and the delta tables carry what moves the glyphs, so a cut keeping one and losing the other is a font with axes that do nothing. Built during planning to confirm it rather than argue it — the shipped cut with gvar dropped and nothing else changed keeps an fvar of exactly 84 bytes and would satisfy any fvar-only check. No length is recorded for a delta table, and that reason is measured too: the same recipe produced a gvar origLength of 70,394 bytes on fontTools 4.60.1 and 70,292 on 4.63.0, so a recorded gvar length would fail a correct build the way a recorded byte count would. Presence and non-zero is the part that is stable.

The recorded fvar length is what gives this teeth against the narrow regression, and those numbers were measured: built from the pinned upstream, the face this binder ships carries an fvar of 84 bytes for its two axes, the same cut with opsz pinned and wght left variable carries 56 — one axis record apart — and the cut with both pinned carries no fvar at all. So dropping opsz alone changes the recorded length and fails here.

Negative control: marking any one of the eight variable fails; marking a face variable while recording an fvar length the directory does not report fails; a face marked variable whose recorded fvar length is zero fails rather than passing as agreed; and a synthetic face carrying fvar at the recorded length while omitting a variation table the manifest records fails, which is the fixture that separates this behaviour from one that only counts fvar bytes.

The behaviour's name and docstring claim a variation-axis table and never an optical size, and the docstring records both limits. First: WOFF2 table data is Brotli-compressed and the stdlib has no Brotli, so the presence and recorded size of fvar are readable and the axis TAGS and RANGES are not. Second, and this is the limit the length check does NOT remove: the length pins neither which axes a face has NOR how many. An fvar is 16 bytes plus 20 per axis plus one record per named instance, so axis count trades against instance count — the shipped cut is 84 bytes as two axes with two instances, and a one-axis face with six instances is 84 as well. Both are spec-legal, and the arithmetic is worth spelling out because two reviewers read it as needing a non-standard encoding: instanceSize is 4 + 4*axisCount, or 6 + 4*axisCount when the optional postScriptNameID is present, so the two-axis case is 16 + 40 + 2*14 and the one-axis case is 16 + 20 + 6*8. They differ in that optional field, which is exactly the kind of detail a length check cannot see. The two-axis-two-instance reading of the shipped 84 is measured, not inferred: a cut narrowed to wght 400..497 drops the named instance that falls outside the range and reports an fvar of 70 bytes — one 14-byte record fewer, which is 6 + 4*2 exactly, so the shipped file's instance records do carry postScriptNameID. A re-vendor that swapped one axis for another, or traded an axis against instances, keeps the length and the green. What the length does catch is a flattening that drops an axis without saying so; a flattening declared in the manifest passes here and is visible in the diff instead, which is the honest description of the guarantee. The docstring says plainly that NOTHING in this repository measures optical-sizing behaviour yet, and points at docs/backlog/watch-optical-harness/FINDINGS.md for the work that will. A docstring that hands the claim off to a check that does not exist is worse than one that admits the gap. Negative control: a behaviour name or docstring asserting an optical-size axis or an axis range fails review as an overclaim; renaming the anchor entry so the registry no longer has it fails with validate_plugin.py:363's named error.

Both new names are present in selftest_behaviours.txt and in its two mirrors, and the anchor floor is not vacuous. Anchoring outside the file is what makes deleting a check fail (serve_status.py:7946-7950). Negative control: deleting a registry entry while leaving its anchor line fails with validate_plugin.py:363's named error, and emptying the anchor file fails with :353's vacuous-floor error.

Every canonical file this item changes is byte-identical in both generated mirrors, so uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py --check is clean and _check_vendored_fonts (validate_plugin.py:412) finds no drift across MIRROR_SKILL_ROOTS (:394). Negative control: validate_plugin.py's own 'a font byte-differing in a mirror fails' case (:1055) stays red when a mirror byte is changed.

work_items.title: Replace the two static cuts with a single unpinned cut
work_items.summary: The two shipped Newsreader files were instanced at opsz 18 before subsetting, which is the axis default and why nothing looked broken. This item re-cuts once from the same upstream with the pin removed and wght limited to the two weights the design uses, ships the single file in place of both, and records in the manifest what the cut carries. Three readers that treat a face's weight as a single integer learn a range, the face enumeration drops to seven, and the frozen design reference is repointed and told to stop presenting itself as something that could witness a font difference. What the floor then checks is the fvar entry's presence and recorded length, not which axes produced it.

The page declares it as a single @font-face with font-weight:400 500, and VENDORED_FACES (serve_status.py:124) becomes seven entries whose Newsreader row names a weight range rather than a single weight.

The subsetting contract is honoured as written, not changed: --unicodes=U+0000-00FF,U+2000-206F --layout-features+=tnum --no-hinting --desubroutinize --flavor=woff2 --name-IDs=1,2,3,4,5,6,16,17. Measured during planning, that exact flag set already preserves fvar, gvar, avar, HVAR and STAT — the variations were lost to the fontTools.varLib.instancer step, not to the subsetter, so no new flag is needed. fontTools stays build-time only and enters no shipped script.
contract.regression_risk:
three places read a face's weight as a single integer and must learn the range, and they read from two different sources, so fixing one does not reach the other. _declared_faces (serve_status.py:14603) parses the stylesheet and yields -1 for a font-weight of '400 500'. _vendored_weights (:8557) folds VENDORED_FACES — not the stylesheet — into family -> set of weights, and six checks read that map. Two of them read the weight set and so break on a range object — _c_type_roles_bound (:9632, the faux-bold sweep over every CSS rule) and _c_card_title_serif_step (:14145). Four read only the family key and do not: _c_binder_headline_type_step (:9862) and the three mono checks at :9028, :9983 and :14128. Leave any of them alone and the self-test fails loudly rather than quietly, which is the good case.

The other sharp edge is the frozen design reference. docs/designs/karta-watch-1440x900-light.html:35-40 declares newsreader-400.woff2 and newsreader-500.woff2 by relative path, so deleting those files leaves it pointing at nothing and validate_plugin.py's design-reference check (:823) fails. It is repointed in this item. Repointing it at the page's new face keeps the property that hid this bug in the first place — the reference renders with the page's own fonts, so it can never disagree with the page about them. That is not closed here; it is written into the reference's own header so the next person reading it knows the file is not a font witness.
contract.verification_honesty:
These claims are kept apart, because collapsing them is how a manifest starts looking like a gate. They are not numbered, because the last two rounds each added one and a stated count that drifts is its own small dishonesty.

INTEGRITY of what shipped is checked: the bytes and sha256 of the file on disk match the manifest, and the payload stays under the bound.

PROVENANCE of what it was cut from is recorded, not checked: the upstream commit, source file, source_sha256 and — new here — the fontTools version. Byte-exact reproducibility is NOT claimed, and the version is added because it does not hold: replaying the documented recipe on fontTools 4.60.1 reproduces newsreader-400.woff2's byte count exactly but lands 36 bytes off newsreader-500.woff2. No oracle can confirm the bytes on disk came from that recipe rather than from somewhere else that renders the same.

The AXIS RANGES this contract states — wght 400..500, opsz 6..72 — are recorded and proven nowhere. Reading an axis tag or a range needs the axis records, which needs a font library, which the floor's dependency rule excludes; the fvar length pins a table size and nothing about which axes produced it. A browser can establish the behaviour instead, and during planning one did: the shipped cut returns 194.406 px for a request of opsz 6 and 165.453 px for opsz 72 where a 17..40 cut clamps to 154.141 and 156.641, and it separates weight 500 from weight 400 by 3.812 px where a wght-pinned cut gives 0.000. No item here runs any of that. Those measurements and the brief for the work are in docs/backlog/watch-optical-harness/FINDINGS.md. Until it exists, the ranges in this contract are a description of the build recipe, and this field says so rather than letting the manifest's precision imply a check.

The DELTA TABLES are checked for presence and not for content, and the distinction is the whole of what this buys. gvar, HVAR and avar must each appear in the directory with a non-zero length, which closes a hole review found late: a cut with fvar intact and gvar dropped passed every other assertion here while its outlines did not move at all (measured: 21 sub-pixels of ink change between weight 400 and 500, against 5,234 on the correct cut). What presence does NOT establish is that the deltas inside those tables are non-zero, or that they describe the axes fvar declares. Reading them needs Brotli and is outside the floor. The reason this one was worth closing at the floor when the axis gap was not: it is one more tag from a parse the binder already performs, and — the part that matters — the width-based harness that will close the axis gap CANNOT close this one. HVAR carries the advances, so a gvar-less face separates weight 400 from 500 by the same 4.828 px as a correct one and measures clean.

Smaller than the axis gap but the same shape, and unnamed until review found it: DECODABILITY is not checked either. Every check in this binder reads filenames, manifest hashes, table-directory metadata, CSS URLs and byte counts. None of them decompresses the face or loads it. Bytes with a plausible WOFF2 header, an fvar entry of the recorded length and non-empty gvar, HVAR and avar entries pass everything here while being an unusable font. Closing it needs a decoder — Brotli for the tables, or a browser that renders the page — and both are outside the floor's dependency rule. It is listed in docs/backlog/watch-optical-harness/FINDINGS.md with the rest.

TABLE CONTENT is the general form of the next several gaps, and it is stated as a list rather than discovered one entry at a time, because five review rounds each found one more claim in this contract with no assertion under it and that is a pattern worth closing by enumeration. Everything the floor reads from a WOFF2 file is a directory entry: a tag and a length. Every table's CONTENTS are Brotli-compressed and unreadable here. So the subsetting contract quoted in this item's preserves field was walked clause by clause against the assertion set, and this is the complete result. CHECKED: --flavor=woff2, in that the file parses as WOFF2 and its directory reads; and --no-hinting in its directory-visible half, the absence of all six of the tables fontTools removes for that flag — cvt , cvar, fpgm, prep, hdmx and VDMX — asserted in assertion 11. An earlier draft of this very enumeration named three of them while the assertion named six, which made its own completeness claim false; that is recorded because a list asserting it is complete has to be audited like any other claim. That entry moved out of the disclosed column after review showed the first version of this enumeration had it wrong — it read 'would show only as size', which is true of the per-glyph instructions inside glyf and false of the font-wide hinting tables, which are ordinary directory entries. The instructions themselves stay unchecked. NOT CHECKED, each one a valid decodable font that passes every assertion in this item after its manifest hash and byte count are updated — --unicodes=U+0000-00FF,U+2000-206F, whose glyph-coverage case is spelled out just below; --layout-features+=tnum, where GSUB is a 260-byte directory entry but the features inside it are not readable, and the page sets font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums in six places (serve_status.py:1531, :1710, :1959, :1973, :2005, :4633), so dropping tnum regresses rendered numerals with the floor green; --name-IDs=1,2,3,4,5,6,16,17, where name is a 662-byte entry whose IDs are content; and --desubroutinize, which is a CFF concern and a no-op for this glyf-outline face. Add to that STAT's axis records, named in assertion 10. Closing any of them needs a decoder, and the binder's position is that the floor stays dependency-free and these are disclosed instead.

GLYPH COVERAGE is the one of those worth spelling out, because this item replaces a font. It is recorded and not checked, and it belongs in this list rather than only in the backlog brief, which is where review found it. serve_status.py:115 already records that coverage is a guarantee of the build step and is never read back out of a woff2 because that needs a font library. Nothing here changes that, and this item REPLACES A FONT, which is exactly when coverage regresses. The concrete artifact: take the correct unpinned cut, drop one code point from its cmap, re-encode it as valid WOFF2 and update the manifest's byte count and hash. fvar is still 84 bytes, gvar HVAR and avar are all still non-empty, every assertion in this item passes, and a character the page renders falls back to a system face. This is not the decodability gap wearing another hat — the font is valid and decodes fine; what fails is the subsetting contract in this item's own preserves field, which promises --unicodes=U+0000-00FF,U+2000-206F. It is not closable here for the same reason as the rest: cmap is a directory ENTRY, so the floor can see the table exists, but the code points inside it are compressed table data and reading them needs Brotli. Closing it needs a cmap read against the code points the fixture actually renders in the serif role, which is briefed with the harness work. Naming it here is the difference between a gap that was disclosed and one that happened to be written down somewhere else.

assertions: The fonts directory ships exactly one Newsreader file, named newsreader-var.woff2, and neither newsreader-400.woff2 nor newsreader-500.woff2 remains. Negative control: leaving either static file in place fails.

The manifest marks Newsreader variable, records its fvar table length, records the variation tables the cut carries so the reader has something to hold it to, and states the axes it carries — wght 400..500 and opsz 6..72 — with the family's own metadata no longer claiming the face was instanced to a pinned opsz. The anchored behaviour from woff2-variation-table-reader, unchanged and not rewritten for this item, reads the shipped file's directory and agrees; the six IBM Plex faces stay marked static and still list no fvar. An fvar entry is where this starts and not where it ends — the delta tables that make those axes do anything are assertion 10, and reading this one alone would leave the wrong impression that a table size settles the question.

State the limit rather than let the contract imply more than the gate delivers. What is checked is that the face carries an fvar table OF THE RECORDED SIZE. That is weaker than an axis count, and the arithmetic is why: an fvar is 16 bytes plus 20 per axis plus one record per named instance, and instanceSize is 4 + 4 per axis, or 6 + 4 per axis when the optional postScriptNameID is present. So the shipped cut is 84 bytes as two axes with two instances, and a one-axis face with six instances is 84 as well — both spec-legal. What the length reliably catches is the narrow regression it was chosen for: the same cut of the same upstream with an axis dropped, which moves 84 to 56.

Two things this item does NOT establish, both named here rather than left to be assumed. That the second axis is opsz, and that its range reaches 6 and 72 — reading an axis tag needs Brotli, which the floor excludes. And the wght axis at all, which costs more than the other gap because this change WEAKENS an existing guarantee: today weight 500 is a separate shipped file and cannot be faked, and after this item it is a position on an axis. Measured during planning, a browser separates both cleanly — the shipped cut returns 194.406 px for a request of opsz 6 and 165.453 px for opsz 72 where a 17..40 cut clamps to 154.141 and 156.641, and weight 500 exceeds weight 400 by 3.812 px where a wght-pinned cut gives 0.000 with synthesis off — so the gap is closable and is briefed in docs/backlog/watch-optical-harness/FINDINGS.md. It is not closed here.

Negative control: a build that pins both axes with fontTools.varLib.instancer produces a file with no fvar and fails; a build that pins opsz alone changes the recorded length from 84 bytes to 56 and fails; a recorded length that does not match the directory fails; and a manifest still carrying a pinned_axes opsz value for Newsreader fails. A cut limited to opsz 17..40 keeps two axes and an fvar of the same recorded length, so it passes everything here — that one is the gap, not a control. And it is only the nearest example of the gap rather than its shape: an 84-byte fvar is equally blind to which axis TAGS are present (wght plus wdth would do), to the RANGES on them, to the named instances' COORDINATES, and to whether postScriptNameID is present at all. Four dimensions, none anchored, and naming only the opsz one would leave a reader thinking the others were covered.

A face's weight becomes range-valued in exactly one place and expanded in exactly one other, and this assertion fixes the shape because getting either end wrong breaks a different check. _declared_faces (serve_status.py:14603) keeps yielding ONE descriptor per @font-face rule — seven, not eight — whose weight field is a normalised range rather than the -1 its weight.isdigit() branch yields today for '400 500'. VENDORED_FACES (:124) carries the same shape in its Newsreader row, so _c_vendored_font_faces (:14665) still compares seven against seven against seven. _vendored_weights (:8557) is the ONE place a range becomes integers: it folds VENDORED_FACES — not the stylesheet — into family -> set of weights, and must expand the range so Newsreader reports {400, 500}.

Its six consumers split two ways, and the split is why only one function has to change. Two read the weight SET and break on a range object: _c_type_roles_bound (:9632, reading at :9657), which sweeps every CSS rule for a numeric font-weight the plugin ships no file for — the faux-bold guard, and the one with the widest reach; and _c_card_title_serif_step (:14145, reading at :14167). Four read only the family KEY and are untouched by the value's shape: _c_binder_headline_type_step (:9862, reading at :9878) and the three mono checks at :9028, :9983 and :14128. Naming that split matters because a builder who fixes _vendored_weights and then checks the headline step will see it green and conclude the change landed, when the headline step would have been green either way.

Negative control: expanding the range inside _declared_faces instead yields eight declared descriptors against seven enumerated and fails _c_vendored_font_faces; leaving _vendored_weights folding a range object into a set of ints fails _c_type_roles_bound and _c_card_title_serif_step while _c_binder_headline_type_step still passes; leaving the stylesheet parse at -1 fails _c_vendored_font_faces on declared-versus-enumerated.

The stylesheet declares one Newsreader @font-face whose font-weight is the range '400 500', VENDORED_FACES (serve_status.py:124) enumerates seven faces, and _c_vendored_font_faces (:14665) reads the same seven from the enumeration, the manifest and the stylesheet — the count still a length, never a number typed twice. Negative control: a manifest still listing eight face entries fails, and a stylesheet still carrying two Newsreader rules fails.

The manifest's bytes and sha256 for the new face match the file on disk, and the total shipped woff2 payload stays under FONT_BUDGET_BYTES (serve_status.py:130). What is asserted is the BOUND, not a byte count, because the count is not stable: replaying the documented recipe produced 79,784 bytes on fontTools 4.60.1 and then 79,948 and 79,648 on two runs of 4.63.0. Against a 409,600-byte bound the shipped total moves from 110,924 to roughly 152,000 either way — about 37 percent — so the bound is the part worth gating and the count is the part worth recording. Negative control: a manifest byte count that disagrees with the file on disk fails _c_font_manifest_agreement (:14687), and a padded extra woff2 fails _c_font_payload_budget (:14713).

The manifest's provenance block is complete and internally consistent — present, well-formed, and agreeing with the pins recorded elsewhere in the manifest. Not verified: no check here confirms the recorded upstream was the actual source, and the honesty field says so. What is asserted is the block's completeness and consistency: the upstream commit 352f6b7d9d6cc4fa9e242b931291d31b21a6dc84, the source file Newsreader[opsz,wght].ttf, the source_sha256 8a08d13f8a6c0d51be379a60af84f945f65369a67e509ee3c3bdcc421254d7c1 — all three verified during planning by downloading that exact file, whose digest agrees — plus the fontTools version the cut was made with, which is new. The version is added because the recipe is not reproducible, measured above. Negative control: a manifest whose subsetting block omits the fontTools version fails, one whose version field is empty fails rather than passing as present, and a Newsreader entry whose source_sha256 or upstream commit differs from the recorded pin fails.

Nothing on the page reaches a font host and the shipped cut is SERVED from /assets/fonts/ with the hub key — served, not loaded, because nothing here decodes it: _c_no_remote_fetch (serve_status.py:14747) and _c_font_src_same_origin (:14761) both pass unchanged. Matching the design means matching what is rendered, not how it is fetched, and the remote link stays out. Negative control: the planted fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet at :14742-14744 still fails the check, and rewriting the face's src to a gstatic URL still fails the second.

The frozen design reference at docs/designs/karta-watch-1440x900-light.html:35-40 declares the same single cut and holds no URL for a file this item deleted. Its header gains a sentence recording that because the file points at the page's own faces it cannot witness a font difference, and naming docs/backlog/watch-optical-harness/FINDINGS.md as where the check that can is briefed — not naming a script that does not exist, because a caveat that points at nothing reads as reassurance. That sentence is enforced, not left to a reviewer's judgement: validate_plugin.py's design-reference check gains a case requiring the header to carry it, so deleting the caveat fails the floor the same way a dangling asset does. Negative control: leaving either deleted URL in the reference fails the existing dangling-asset case (:823); removing the caveat sentence fails the new one; and a reference whose header still presents the file as a complete fidelity witness cannot pass both.

Both generated mirrors of every canonical file this item changes are byte-identical, so uv run scripts/sync_codex_skills.py --check is clean and _check_vendored_fonts (validate_plugin.py:412) finds no drift across MIRROR_SKILL_ROOTS (:394). Negative control: validate_plugin.py's own 'a font byte-differing in a mirror fails' case (:1055) stays red when a mirror byte is changed.

The shipped face's table directory lists the variation tables the manifest records, each with a non-zero recorded origLength — gvar, HVAR and avar, and with them STAT — read by the same woff2-variation-table-reader parse that reads fvar, so this costs no new dependency and stays inside the floor's rule. This assertion exists because review found a build that passes every other assertion in this item while reproducing the exact defect the item was written to fix, and the file was then built to confirm it rather than argued about: take the correct cut, drop gvar alone, and the result keeps fvar at 84 bytes, keeps the manifest agreement, keeps the recorded axes, and passes assertions 1 through 9 without a single change to them. Note which direction the size moves, because it is why the payload assertion can never catch this: built as a clean pair through one save path so gvar is the only difference, the correct cut is 79,920 bytes and the gvar-less one is 40,148 — the broken file is HALF the size and a budget bound is an upper bound, so it clears more easily than the correct one. What it does not do is vary. Measured in Chromium at 200px on 'Hamb', ink coverage moves from 23,240 to 28,474 sub-pixels between weight 400 and 500 on the correct cut — and from 17,908 to 17,929 on the gvar-less one, a delta of 21 against 5,234. The letterforms are frozen. The trap worth naming: the ADVANCES still move, because HVAR carries those and HVAR survived, so the same probe measured by WIDTH reports an identical 4.828 px separation for both files and calls the broken one correct. That is why this is a directory assertion and not something left to the width harness briefed in docs/backlog/watch-optical-harness/FINDINGS.md, which cannot see it. Note what is still not established, since presence is not content: a gvar of non-zero length is not proof its deltas are non-zero, and reading them needs Brotli. The four tags are not one kind of thing, and reading them as one would misdescribe what each buys. gvar, HVAR and avar are a fact about THIS cut: they are what the documented recipe preserves from this upstream, measured, and they are required here for that reason rather than because every variable font must carry all three — OpenType requires none of them specifically. STAT is the opposite case and was missed until review found it: OpenType requires a STAT table in every variable font, so a cut without one is non-conforming whatever else it gets right, and this item's own preserves field already claims the flag set keeps it. That was a claim with no check under it — the same shape as the gvar gap, one table over. Measured: STAT is 156 bytes in the shipped cut and 76 in the static faces, so it is present in both and cannot distinguish variable from static. Say exactly what this buys, because the word conformance would overstate it: what is checked is that a REQUIRED TABLE IS PRESENT, not that the font conforms. OpenType also requires each fvar axis to have a matching STAT axis record under the same name ID, and that is table CONTENT, so it needs Brotli and is not checked. A cut whose STAT omits the opsz axis record passes here. It also exercises the reader's literal-tag path, since STAT is not in the WOFF2 known-tag list and always arrives as four literal bytes. Negative control: the gvar-dropped cut described above fails this assertion and only this one; a manifest marking Newsreader variable while the file lists no gvar fails; a cut with only STAT removed — every other table untouched, manifest hash and byte count updated — fails here and nowhere else; and restoring each passes. No length is recorded for any of the three, because the same recipe gave gvar 70,394 bytes on fontTools 4.60.1 and 70,292 on 4.63.0 — pinning it would fail a correct build.

The shipped cut's directory lists NONE of the six font-wide hinting tables — cvt , cvar, fpgm, prep, hdmx and VDMX — which is the directory-visible half of the recipe's --no-hinting flag. Review filed this flag as uncheckable on the reasoning that hinting 'would show only as size'; that was wrong, and the correction is the reason this assertion exists. --no-hinting does two things: it strips the per-glyph instructions, which live inside glyf and are compressed and therefore genuinely out of reach here, and it drops the font-wide hinting TABLES, which are directory entries like any other. The list is fontTools' own, not a guess: _hinting_tables_default in fontTools.subset is [cvt, cvar, fpgm, prep, hdmx, VDMX], matched after a tag strip so cvt with its trailing space is covered, and an earlier draft of this assertion named only three of them. Measured rather than assumed: of the six, the pinned upstream Newsreader carries prep alone, and every cut built with the documented flags — the two static faces shipping today included — lists none of the six. So prep is the tag with a live negative control on this upstream and the other five are guards that cost nothing and catch a changed upstream or a changed recipe. cvar is the one worth naming: it is the variation of cvt, so it is the member of this set most likely to appear in a variable cut. So a cut built without --no-hinting keeps prep, and before this assertion it passed everything. State the limit in the same breath: absence of the tables does NOT establish that the glyph instructions were stripped, since those are compressed content. The tables are the part that is visible, so the tables are the part that is asserted. Negative control: a cut rebuilt without --no-hinting retains prep and fails here and nowhere else; adding any of the six tags to the shipped face fails; and the six IBM Plex faces, which list none of them either, stay passing.
